titles: CHAPTER TWO. On the immortality of the soul, from the light of nature and the confession of barbarians, both ancient and recently discovered
II. By the light of nature: Gentiles both barbarians and philosophers acknowledge immortality and care about the soul's state after this life
III-IV. Barbarians ancient and recent; the ancient Getae and Egyptians (Herodotus, Diodorus)
V. Recently discovered peoples listed; whether the West Indies were known to the ancients; Fathers denied antipodes
Yet the New World may long have been partly known; Besoldus; Japheth origin; Fuller and others
VI. The Guineans on another life and the last judgment; burial goods and royal funerary sacrifice
VII. The Chinese: pagan religion; immortality and retribution; magnificent tombs (Linschoten)
VIII. The Peruvians: immortality, eternal life and damnation (Acosta); ignorance of bodily resurrection; funerary slaves (Benzoni)
IX-X. Mexicans profess the same faith; Guianans agree with Peruvians (Raleigh); burial with wives and treasures
XI. The Tupinamba of Brazil: fierce cannibals who believe soul-immortality; Lery on virtue, paradise, and Aygnan
XII. The Virginians also believe soul-immortality; transfer to gods' seats or Popogusso (Hariot)
XIII. What barbarian confession shows: universal natural consensus; true light overlaid with false, vain, and impious additions — Cap. 2 close
